source_refs.note: Book p. 12: 1.4.1 Properties of Cube Roots of Unity (i)-(iii)

items.title: 1.4.1 Properties of Cube Roots of Unity

blocks.text: (i) Each complex cube root of unity is square of the other
and if \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = \omega\), then \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = \omega^{2}\) [\(\omega\) is read as omega]

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The second line repeats the first root. It should read: if \(\frac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = \omega\), then \(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = \omega^{2}\). Whichever complex root we call \(\omega\), the other one is \(\omega^{2}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Why property (i) is true:
\[\left(\dfrac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)^{2} = \dfrac{1 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i + 3i^{2}}{4}\]
\[= \dfrac{-2 - 2\sqrt{3}\,i}{4} = \dfrac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\]
In the same way \(\left(\frac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2}\). So the three cube roots of unity are \(1, \omega, \omega^{2}\).
(ii) The sum of all the three cube roots of unity is zero

blocks.text_alt: 1 plus omega plus omega squared equals 0

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Why: \(1 + \frac{-1+\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} + \frac{-1-\sqrt{3}\,i}{2} = 1 + \frac{-2}{2} = 0\). Another way: \(\omega\) is a root of \(x^{2} + x + 1 = 0\), so \(\omega^{2} + \omega + 1 = 0\). Useful forms: \(\omega + \omega^{2} = -1\), \(1 + \omega = -\omega^{2}\), \(1 + \omega^{2} = -\omega\).
(iii) The product of all the three cube roots of unity is unity

blocks.text_alt: 1 times omega times omega squared equals omega cubed equals 1

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Why: \(\omega\) is a cube root of 1, so \(\omega^{3} = 1\) by definition. Directly: \(\omega \cdot \omega^{2} = \frac{(-1)^{2} - (\sqrt{3}\,i)^{2}}{4} = \frac{1 + 3}{4} = 1\). Because \(\omega^{3} = 1\), any power of \(\omega\) can be reduced: divide the exponent by 3 and keep the remainder.

blocks.caption: Powers of ω repeat in a cycle of 3

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: To simplify \(\omega^{28}\): \(28 = 3 \times 9 + 1\), so \(\omega^{28} = (\omega^{3})^{9}\omega = \omega\). Replace \(1 + \omega\) by \(-\omega^{2}\) and \(\omega + \omega^{2}\) by \(-1\) whenever they appear.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. The cube roots of unity are \(1, \omega, \omega^{2}\); each complex root is the square of the other.
2. \(1 + \omega + \omega^{2} = 0\).
3. \(\omega^{3} = 1\), so powers of \(\omega\) repeat every 3.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Thinking \(\omega\) is one fixed root only: either complex root can be called \(\omega\); the other is then \(\omega^{2}\).
2. Writing \(1 + \omega + \omega^{2} = 1\) (confusing the sum with the product).
3. Reducing \(\omega^{n}\) by dividing \(n\) by 2 instead of 3.
